name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,431

clue.text: Drink somehow got paler

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unstated route, so they are rearranged rather than read in order

blocks.note: eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sips a drink and somehow turns pale, as if feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: A lager top is a pint of lager with a splash of lemonade on top, a British pub order.
explanation.definitionFit: A lager top is a pub beverage: beer topped with a little lemonade, so it is one kind of alcoholic refreshment.

clue.text: Grotty station

blocks.note: first meaning: foul, nasty, offensive
second meaning: position or standing in a hierarchy

explanation.surface: A run-down, grubby railway stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a dirty railway stop; 'station' really means social standing. Grotty is British slang for shabby or unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means smelly or foul; as a noun it means one's social position or military grade.

clue.text: Historian accepting queen's badge

indicators.note: the historian accepting something takes it in, so the other piece goes inside his name

blocks.note: Livy was the Roman historian of Rome's early centuries
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: An old historian is handed a royal emblem by the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: LIV(ER)Y. The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the distinctive uniform or insignia worn by servants or members of a guild, marking whom they belong to, like an emblem.

clue.text: Officer drinking a French wine with catholic artist

indicators.note: the officer drinking something swallows it, so the drink sits inside his title

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, a police officer
taken as written
vin is the French word for wine
C is the standard abbreviation for Catholic

explanation.surface: A police officer drinks French wine in the company of a Catholic painter.
explanation.walkthrough: D(A VIN)I then C; 'with' simply adds C at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Italian Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper.

clue.text: Wise man taking medicine for problem with waterworks?

indicators.note: the wise man taking his medicine takes it in, so it goes inside him

blocks.note: a sage is a wise man
a pill is a dose of medicine

explanation.surface: An old man takes tablets for a bladder complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waterworks' is slang for the urinary system, which the surface leans on; the question mark warns that here it means a leak of water, as from a mains or a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A spillage is liquid escaping where it should not, the kind of mishap a plumbing system or tank might suffer.

clue.text: Trace antelope roaming Ecuador's last remote area

indicators.note: last asks for only the final letter of the country's name
roaming means wandering about, so these letters move out of their order

blocks.note: a trace or tiny amount is a hint
the eland is a large African antelope
final letter of Ecuador

explanation.surface: A faint sign of an antelope wandering a far-off region of Ecuador.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinterland is the backcountry lying far from coasts and cities, a distant thinly settled region.

clue.text: Fine yarn spun in Rome

indicators.note: spun means twisted round, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Delicate thread being spun in a workshop in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spun' fits the yarn picture perfectly, which hides its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Merino is soft wool from the merino breed of sheep, prized for knitting thread because it is so soft.

clue.text: Song by girl after drink

indicators.note: after places the girl's name behind the drink in the finished word

blocks.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
Tina, a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl sings a song once she has had a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavatina is a short simple operatic aria or melody, so it is a piece for singing.

clue.text: Poet's first poem is excellent

indicators.note: first asks for just the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: opening letter of Poet
rime is an old spelling of rhyme, a poem, as in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner

explanation.surface: A critic declares that a poet's debut poem is superb.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime describes something of top quality, as in prime beef, the best grade available.

clue.text: Bonus for each £1000?

blocks.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
K stands for a thousand, as in a salary of 30K

explanation.surface: A worker wonders whether a bonus comes at a fixed rate for every thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk is a perquisite, an extra benefit received on top of a salary such as a company car.

clue.text: Malfunctioning toilets contain animal's body part

indicators.note: something malfunctioning is out of order, so these letters are jumbled
to contain is to hold inside, so the jumble goes around the creature

blocks.note: taken as written
a pig is a farm animal

explanation.surface: Broken lavatories trap an animal's carcass, a grim plumbing tale.
explanation.walkthrough: E(PIG)LOTTIS. The 's reads as 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The epiglottis is the flap of cartilage at the root of the tongue that covers the windpipe when swallowing, an anatomical organ.

clue.text: Policeman close to adversary like Scrooge?

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

blocks.note: Sting was the singer of the band The Police, so he is a 'policeman'
final letter of adversary

explanation.surface: A constable gets near to an enemy who resembles the miser of Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policeman' is a pun: Sting fronted the rock band The Police. The question mark marks Scrooge as an example of the quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge in Dickens's A Christmas Carol is the archetypal miser, mean and tight-fisted with money.

clue.text: Nuclear engineer swore about list in US city

indicators.note: read as a verb, to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the following word's letters are rearranged
about means going around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for nuclear
taken as written
a ship that lists leans to one side

explanation.surface: A nuclear engineer cursed over a checklist while working in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuclear engineer' looks like one person giving NE; only 'Nuclear' gives a letter, and 'engineer' is a verb telling you to rework the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: New Orleans is the Louisiana port on the Mississippi, birthplace of jazz, an American metropolis.

clue.text: Setter leaving threesome in awfully macho forum

indicators.note: the setter leaving the group means he drops out of it and is removed
in places what remains of the group inside the other letters
awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters come out in a mangled order

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself as I
a trio is a group of three
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter walks out of a menage a trois in a terribly blokey online discussion group.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the clue's own author, who calls himself I; he leaves the group of three before what is left goes inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatroom is an online space where people post messages and discuss topics, a modern version of a public meeting place for debate.

clue.text: Running stitches protect top of pocket

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
to protect is to shield by surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: sewing is the work of making stitches
opening letter of pocket

explanation.surface: A tailor's running stitch reinforces the opening of a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running stitches' looks like a single sewing term, but 'Running' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spewing means gushing or pouring out in a stream, as liquid running from a burst pipe.

clue.text: After prison chap returned with Eastern alias

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the prison word
returned means sent back, so the chap is read from right to left

blocks.note: nick is British slang for prison or a police station
a chap is a man
E is the abbreviation for Eastern

explanation.surface: A man comes back from jail with an assumed Oriental name.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname is an informal name used in place of the real one, so it is another name a person goes by.

clue.text: Knight following sign outside bar to Asian republic

indicators.note: the sign sitting outside means it wraps around the next piece
following places the knight after the rest in the finished word

blocks.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
to bar is to ban
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight trails a pub sign on his way to an Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: LE(BAN)O then N. In chess notation N is used for the knight because K is taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a Middle Eastern republic on the Mediterranean, and the Middle East lies in western Asia.

clue.text: Soil treated to beat risk to wildlife

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are changed in order

blocks.note: taken as written
to lick is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: Ground treated with chemicals to defeat a hazard to animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilled crude oil floating on the sea coats seabirds and marine creatures, a notorious environmental danger to animals.

clue.text: Gaul finds upturned Greek letter under flower

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the letter below the flower, so it comes second
in a down entry, upturned means turned upside down, so the letter is read bottom to top

blocks.note: the aster is a daisy-like flower
xi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Frenchman of old discovers a Greek inscription upside down beneath a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaul' looks like a country or region, but it means a man from Gaul.
explanation.definitionFit: Asterix is the comic-book hero of Goscinny and Uderzo, a warrior from a village in ancient Gaul resisting the Romans.

clue.text: Moulds made by retired sailors involved in horrible crimes

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
involved in means wrapped up inside, so one piece sits within the other
horrible suggests something ugly and misshapen, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken loosely for two-letter abbreviation, retired to give AT
taken as written

explanation.surface: Casting moulds were made by old seamen mixed up in dreadful offences.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters for 'sailors' are a loose fit: the usual abbreviation that reverses to them stands for the Territorial Army, soldiers rather than seamen, so this looks like a slip by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A matrix is a mould in which type or a coin is cast, and matrices is its plural.

clue.text: Steers clear of space in hollow asbestos

indicators.note: a hollow word has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters
in places the space inside the remaining letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of asbestos
a void is an empty space

explanation.surface: Someone keeps away from a cavity filled with asbestos, wisely.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to keep away from it or dodge it, matching the idiom for staying away.

clue.text: Duke and duchess kept in line by cook

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the titled pair sit within the line

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Duke
D is the abbreviation for Duchess
a file is a line, as in single file

explanation.surface: An aristocratic couple are kept in a queue by their chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the chef in the scene, but it is the verb, as in to cook the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle accounts is to falsify them dishonestly, the same as the slang sense of cooking figures.

clue.text: Place turning up in extremely foolish fixation

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means rising from the bottom, so the place is read backwards
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those letters are kept
in places the reversed place inside the two kept letters

blocks.note: a site is a place
first and last letters of foolish

explanation.surface: Somewhere appears within a terribly silly obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is an obsessive attachment or preoccupation, the same as an abnormal fixation on something.

clue.text: Something finally finished by new people with time to rule

indicators.note: finally asks for only the last letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: last letter of Something
something over is finished
N is the abbreviation for new
men are people
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A job is at last completed by fresh staff, given enough time to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Government is the act of governing, so as a noun it is the same as rule or administration of a country.

clue.text: Oboist originally leaving instrument in part of prison

indicators.note: originally points to the very first letter of the player's title
leaving says that letter departs from the instrument and is removed

blocks.note: opening letter of Oboist
a cello is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: An oboe player abandons his instrument in a jail block.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is the small room where a prisoner is locked up, one section of a jail.

clue.text: Compiler's first music is rubbish!

indicators.note: first asks for just the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: opening letter of Compiler
rap is a genre of music

explanation.surface: A setter shrugs that his debut album is garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Crap is vulgar slang for worthless nonsense or junk, so it means something of no value.

clue.text: Fellows losing money in dark fabric

indicators.note: the fellows losing something means a letter is taken away from them
in places what remains of the fellows inside the dark word

blocks.note: fellows are men
M is the abbreviation for money
dim means dark or poorly lit

explanation.surface: Penniless men in a sombre cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark' looks like a colour describing the cloth, but it is wordplay; only the last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is the hard-wearing twilled cotton cloth used for jeans, a type of textile.

clue.text: Intoxicated leaders can set bad example

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the word's opening letters are kept
bad suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: the first two letters of Intoxicated
six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Drunken bosses are a poor role model for their staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' is plural, so it takes the first two letters rather than one.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or occurrence of something, used to illustrate a point the way an example does.
